clues.title: Plate: fully blue plate
text: Senegal is the only African country to use fully **blue** licence plates. A newer version exists in Generation 4 which looks like the standard **European** licence plate which is white with a blue strip on the left.
clues.summary: The only African country with fully blue licence plates. Newer plates in Gen 4 coverage look like the standard European plate: white with a blue strip on the left.

clues.title: Google car: silver or white truck cab (Gen 4)
text: A **silver** or **white** truck cab is visible in the Generation 4 coverage. Several variants of each exist, most of which are region or road specific. The most useful and recognizable ones will be shown in the spotlight section. For a complete overview, see [this document](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JdyJNoOkksLAdGnJ_scA17K1pHV3THHERY-Y05B6rKI/edit#gid=0) by Lupus.
In the area around Dakar and Thies you can also find a [black](https://maps.app.goo.gl/M993iFkmA7pFDR2k7) pick up truck.
NOTE: The car may sometimes be fully blurred. Make sure to look at the landscape or other clues in the absence of car meta.

images.caption: Two car roofs labelled Silver (left) and White (right)

clues.summary: Gen 4 coverage shows a silver or white truck cab, in several variants that are mostly tied to certain regions or roads. Near the capital there is also a black pick-up. The car can be fully blurred, so check the landscape too.

clues.title: Google car: roof rack and right mirror, Gen 3
text: A Google Car with a visible **roof rack** and the right side mirror is seen in Generation 3 coverage. **Rifts** can also be seen in the sky.
NOTE: This specific Google Car with the right side mirror visible is unique to Senegal. Roof racks and rifts however can be seen in various other countries.

images.caption: Red circle zooms in on the right mirror at the top right of the blur

clues.summary: In Gen 3 coverage you can see the roof rack and the right side mirror, plus rifts in the sky. The visible mirror is unique to this country, but roof racks and rifts appear elsewhere.

clues.title: Driving side: right
text: Senegal drives on the **right**.
NOTE: This is mostly useful to distinguish it from Kenya, which drives on the left. The other countries with coverage in Africa that drive on the right are Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tunisia.

images.caption: Road with cars on the right; an overlaid two-way traffic warning sign marks the driving side

clues.summary: Traffic drives on the right. Useful against Kenya, which drives on the left. Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tunisia also drive on the right.

clues.title: Road items: French-style bollards, poles, signs
text: Being a former French colony, Senegal uses French infrastructure such as **bollards**, **poles**, **signs** and **road** **lines**.
clues.summary: As a former French colony, it uses French-style bollards, poles, signs and road lines.

clues.title: Language: French
text: The official and most common language seen in Senegal is French.
NOTE: The other sub-Saharan countries with street view coverage use English (Rwanda being a minor exception to this – however landscape should be sufficient to always tell the difference).
clues.summary: The main language on signs is French. Other sub-Saharan countries with coverage use English, apart from Rwanda, where the landscape tells them apart.

differs.how: Rwanda also has some French but looks very different

clues.title: Km marker: white with red top, towns listed
text: The road number and the distance to the nearest towns can be seen on these white **kilometre markers** with a red top.
NOTE: The town that is the furthest distance away is usually the largest.
clues.summary: White kilometre markers with a red top, showing the road number and distances to nearby towns. The farthest town listed is usually the largest.

clues.title: Sign: white town sign, thick pink outline
text: Most town entry signs in Senegal are white and feature a **thick pink** outline. The town is also written in a bold, black font.
clues.summary: Most town entry signs are white with a thick pink outline and the town name in bold black letters.

clues.title: Street lamps: black with solar panel on top
text: These simple **black lamps** with a **solar panel** at the top are commonly seen in Senegal.

images.caption: Black street lamp with a solar panel on top

clues.summary: Simple black lamp posts with a solar panel on top are common.

clues.title: Taxis: yellow-orange with black fenders
text: **Yellow-orange** taxis with **black fenders** can commonly be seen in Senegal.
clues.summary: Yellow-orange taxis with black fenders are common.

clues.title: Coverage: mostly west, few side roads in east
text: This is a **coverage map** of Senegal. Most of the coverage is west of Touba, with very few roads apart from main roads covered in the east.

_You can click on the image to enlarge it. Alternatively, you can look at the coverage in more detail [on this site](https://sv-map.netlify.app#base=roadmap&cov=official&zoom=8&center=14.549025564638553%2C-14.287719726562502)._
clues.summary: Most coverage is in the west. In the east only the main roads are covered.

clues.title: Landscape: flat, dry savannah, short pale trees
text: The landscape north of The Gambia and for Senegal generally is a **flat, arid, savannah-desert** landscape with sparse trees. The trees themselves will be somewhat short and have leaves that are faded in colour.
clues.summary: Flat, dry savannah-desert with sparse, fairly short trees whose leaves are faded in colour. This is the look for most of the country.

clues.title: Vegetation: lush and green, palms near coast
text: The vegetation in the region south of The Gambia is more lush and green compared to the rest of Senegal, and palm trees can be seen closer to the coast.

NOTE: Coverage toward the west will also be [especially tropical](https://goo.gl/maps/52g1NQ7hwGZtNejD8). In addition, make sure not to confuse the south with some coverage near Dakar, which can look deceivingly green. However, here the vegetation will look a lot more [low and coastal](https://goo.gl/maps/oouBBYadRN3oiSRi8).
clues.summary: In the far south, vegetation is much greener and more lush than elsewhere, with palm trees near the coast. Don't confuse it with the greenish coast near the capital, where plants look lower.

clues.title: Coverage: sandy road with sparse trees
text: Diourbel Region is the only region in Senegal with extensive **rural coverage**. The coverage in the region will look like this, with the Google Car driving on a sandy road with sparse trees. Some of the coverage extends to the west in the Thies region up to Babou.
NOTE: The sand in the coverage around Touba tends to be more [grassy](https://goo.gl/maps/BWCDdy4HBumDShTx9).
clues.summary: The only region with plenty of rural coverage: the car drives on sandy roads with sparse trees. Sand near the big holy city is more grassy.

clues.title: Landscape: gently rolling vegetated dunes
text: A **very slightly rolling** landscape consisting of vegetated sand dunes can be seen along the northwestern coast.
clues.summary: Very slightly rolling land of vegetated sand dunes along the northwest coast.

clues.title: Landscape: dry with slight hills
text: A **dry** landscape with **slight hills** can mostly be seen around Bakel, but also south to Nayé.
clues.summary: A dry landscape with slight hills, mostly in the far east and a bit south of it.

clues.title: Landscape: greener with bigger hills
text: A **greener** landscape with **larger hills** can be seen around Kedougou and Mako.
clues.summary: In the southeast: a greener landscape with larger hills.

clues.title: Fields: irrigated rice
text: **Irrigated rice fields** can sometimes be seen in the region between St Louis and Richard Toll.
clues.summary: Irrigated rice fields can sometimes be seen in the north, between two towns near the river.

clues.title: Google car: silver Gen 4
text: The silver Generation 4 car with a **long antenna** at the front left can be seen on many roads, but none past the eastern border of Diourbel Region.
NOTE: The antenna is visible even if the car is [blurred](https://goo.gl/maps/kPSPK8pH463oWffJ7).
clues.summary: Silver Gen 4 truck with a long antenna at the front left, found on many roads but not past the eastern edge of one central region. The antenna shows even when the car is blurred.

clues.title: Google car: plain white Gen 4
text: The regular Generation 4 **white car** is most commonly found south of The Gambia, but can also be found on the northeastern coast and a small region between Kaolack and Saly.
clues.summary: The regular white Gen 4 car is mostly in the south, but also on the northeast coast and in one small western area.

clues.title: Road: divided highway, no road number
text: **Divided highways** are found between Dakar and Touba. The two divided highways are between Dakar and Touba, and between Dakar and Saly.
NOTE: On Google Maps, the road shows as a yellow road but without road number. There are also no divided highways in Generation 3.
clues.summary: Divided highways only exist between the capital and the holy city, and between the capital and a coastal town. On Google Maps they are yellow roads with no number, and none exist in Gen 3.

clues.title: Road: runs northeast, railway alongside
text: The N1 between Tambacounda and Nayé generally runs in a **northeast east** direction. A **railway** runs parallel to the road. The railway is to the south of the road between Tambacounda to just before Youpe Amadi, and is to the north from Youpe Amadi to Bellé.
clues.summary: A road running roughly northeast with a railway beside it. The railway is south of the road at first, then switches to the north.

clues.title: Coverage: hazy, low sun, some farmland
text: **Hazy** coverage with a **low sun** through a sometimes agricultural landscape can be seen on the N2 between St. Louis and Richard Toll.
clues.summary: Hazy coverage with a low sun, passing through partly farmed land, on the main road in the far north.

clues.title: Landscape: wide road, desert
text: The N2 between Richard Toll and Matam is a wide road going through a flat desert landscape with very sparse trees. It can be recognized by the **bright blue skies** with **no clouds**. The road itself goes west-east and northwest-southeast.
NOTE: The higher the sun is, the more east you are.
clues.summary: A wide road through flat desert with very few trees and bright blue, cloudless skies. The higher the sun, the further east you are.

clues.title: Roadside: tall bright yellow grass patches
text: Distinct, tall patches of **bright yellow grass** can be seen along the N3, mostly to the east in the Matam Region.

images.caption: Tall bright yellow grass beside the road

clues.summary: Distinct tall patches of bright yellow grass beside the road, mostly in the east.

clues.title: Coverage: hazy bushfire smoke
text: The road northeast of Kedougou to the Malian border can be recognized by the **hazy bushfire** coverage. Smoke trails can sometimes be seen in the distance. The road is paved south of Saraya.
clues.summary: A road in the southeast with hazy bushfire coverage, sometimes smoke trails in the distance. It is paved in the southern part.

clues.title: Landscape: flat, slightly marshy, low plants
text: A flat, **slightly marshy** landscape with low vegetation can be seen on a few sections of roads in the Saloum River Delta.
clues.summary: A flat, slightly marshy landscape with low vegetation on a few roads in a river delta.

clues.title: Coverage: dirt road in evening light
text: The Kola-Velingara road between Saré Amirou and Badion is a dirt road that can be recognized by the **late afternoon** to **evening** coverage. The coverage gets later toward the west.
clues.summary: A dirt road shot in late afternoon to evening light, getting later towards the west.

clues.title: Road: bright orange dirt, dry brown hills, haze
text: The white road in the Forest of Thies can be recognized by the **dry**,** slightly hilly** landscape with brown vegetation. The road itself is made of bright orange dirt. There is also a noticeably haze in the coverage.
clues.summary: A white-looking road of bright orange dirt through a dry, slightly hilly landscape with brown vegetation and noticeable haze.

clues.title: City: dense, tall modern buildings
text: Dakar is the **largest** and **capital city** of Senegal. It can be recognized by the denseness of the city and taller, more modern buildings.
clues.summary: The capital is the biggest city, with dense streets and taller, more modern buildings.

clues.title: Landmark: mosque with five tall minarets
text: The [**infamous**](https://youtu.be/r6PWu8A72oI?t=697)** Great Mosque of Touba** can be recognized by the five tall minarets, which can be seen from [afar](https://goo.gl/maps/MnTgaEw4r6mCQm9U9).

images.caption: A mosque with five tall minarets

clues.summary: A famous mosque in the holy city has five tall minarets and can be seen from far away.

clues.title: Bollard: round white post, pointed top, band
text: The Senegal/French bollard is extremely recognizable and appears very often. It is a round white post with a pointed top and a reflector band going all the way around. The band can be grey or red. Some rare variations have a fully red top.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Very common round white post with a pointed top and a reflector band all the way round, grey or red. A rare version has a fully red top. It is the French-style bollard.

clues.title: Google car: silver Gen 4 with box on back right
text: The silver Generation 4 car with a box in the back right of the cab can mainly be seen on the road between Richard Toll and Louga, and the N3 between Tiourene and Matam. It can also be seen on the dirt road hugging the Mauritanian border, from Matam to Gassamberi. Finally, it can be seen on a few roads near Diolotène.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Silver Gen 4 truck with a box at the back right of the cab. Seen mainly on roads in the north and along the dirt road beside the northern border, plus a few other roads.

clues.title: Google car: silver Gen 4, stain back left
text: The silver Generation 4 car with a stain at the back left of the cab can be seen on the N2 from Richard Toll to Matam and Bakel to Nayé. It can also be seen on the N1 between Tambacounda and Nayé.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Silver Gen 4 truck with a stain at the back left of the cab, seen in the north and east.

clues.title: Google car: silver Gen 4, stain and dirty roof
text: The silver Generation 4 car with a stain at the back left and a dirty roof can mainly be seen on the N1 between Kaffrine and Tambacounda, and the N7 between Tambacounda and Kedougou. It can also be seen between Dahra and Diakhao.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Silver Gen 4 truck with a stain at the back left and a dirty roof, seen mainly on main roads in the centre and southeast.

clues.title: Google car: silver Gen 4, red cloth front left
text: The silver Generation 4 car with a red cloth at the front left can be seen on this eastern road between Ouro Sogui and Bakel.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Silver Gen 4 truck with a red cloth at the front left, seen on one road in the northeast.

clues.title: Google car: white Gen 4, antenna folded flat
text: The white Generation 4 car but with the antenna down, parallel to the car’s roof, can be found on the N6 between Ziguinchor and Kolda.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: White Gen 4 car with the antenna laid down parallel to the roof, seen on one road in the south.

clues.title: Google car: white Gen 4, dirty back
text: The white Generation 4 car with a noticeably dirty back can be seen on the road going north of Kolda, up to Katonfara.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: White Gen 4 car with a noticeably dirty back, seen on a road in the south.
